card.name: Words just before US park and trail names
card.fires_on: Small linking words (the, in, of, like, a comma) right before a national park, trail, or historic site name, in travel and park-service text. Also the digit inside a year in a citation.

modes.label: Before park names
modes.description: A small word such as 'the' or a comma comes just before a named national park, trail, or recreation area.
modes.example: Along with twelve national historic sites, areas, and corridors, the National Park Service also manages the Cape Cod National Seashore and<< the>> Boston Harbor Islands National Recreation Area.

modes.label: Visiting and tours
modes.description: A linking word in a sentence about tours, hikers or visitors going to a site.
modes.example: You can put more pieces into the Missionary Ridge puzzle by following General Sherman's actions in a tour that begins at 2 pm Saturday<< in>> the Tennessee Riverpark.

modes.label: Year digit in citation
modes.description: The digit inside a publication year in a book reference.
modes.example: (Knoxville: University of Tennessee Press, <<1>>998) and Jack B.

card.writes: It pushes toward words like visitor, visitors and ranger, which fit park and tourism text.
card.plain: It spots the small word right before a park or trail name, where a word like visitors or ranger could come next.
